spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m9p3t3 ----
\* A container-ship crane yard hands bay slots to cranes using epoch-numbered reconfiguration.
\* Each slot carries the epoch at which it was last reconfigured. A crane first records a
\* reservation stamped with the slot epoch it observed, then commits only while that stamp still
\* matches the slot's live epoch. A yard reconfiguration bumps the global epoch, re-stamps a slot,
\* and clears whatever was committed on it, so a crane that fell behind (slow but not failed) holds
\* a stale reservation it must drop. No slot is ever left committed under an epoch older than its
\* current reconfiguration epoch, which is what would let a pre- and a post-reconfiguration crane
\* both believe they own the same bay.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Cranes == {"c1", "c2"}
Slots == {"s1", "s2"}
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, slotEpoch, committed, committedEpoch, reserv

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ slotEpoch \in [Slots -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ committed \in [Slots -> Cranes \cup {NONE}]
  /\ committedEpoch \in [Slots -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ reserv \in [Cranes -> [slot: Slots \cup {NONE}, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ slotEpoch = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ committed = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
  /\ committedEpoch = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ reserv = [c \in Cranes |-> [slot |-> NONE, ep |-> 0]]

Reconfig(s) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ slotEpoch' = [slotEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch + 1]
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
  /\ committedEpoch' = [committedEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED reserv

Reserve(c, s) ==
  /\ reserv[c].slot = NONE
  /\ reserv' = [reserv EXCEPT ![c] = [slot |-> s, ep |-> slotEpoch[s]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, slotEpoch, committed, committedEpoch>>

Commit(c, s) ==
  /\ reserv[c].slot = s
  /\ committed[s] = NONE
  /\ reserv[c].ep = slotEpoch[s]
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![s] = c]
  /\ committedEpoch' = [committedEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = slotEpoch[s]]
  /\ reserv' = [reserv EXCEPT ![c] = [slot |-> NONE, ep |-> 0]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, slotEpoch>>

Release(c, s) ==
  /\ committed[s] = c
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, slotEpoch, committedEpoch, reserv>>

DropStale(c) ==
  /\ reserv[c].slot # NONE
  /\ reserv[c].ep # slotEpoch[reserv[c].slot]
  /\ reserv' = [reserv EXCEPT ![c] = [slot |-> NONE, ep |-> 0]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, slotEpoch, committed, committedEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Reconfig(s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Slots : Reserve(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Slots : Commit(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, s \in Slots : Release(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : DropStale(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, slotEpoch, committed, committedEpoch, reserv>>

NoStaleAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slots : committed[s] # NONE => committedEpoch[s] = slotEpoch[s]
====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard allocates bay slots to cranes under epoch-numbered reconfiguration. A global epoch counter and a per-slot epoch record which reconfiguration generation each bay currently belongs to. A crane that wants a bay first reserves it, stamping its reservation with the slot epoch it observed at that moment; each crane holds at most one outstanding reservation. To take the bay, the crane commits, but the yard only honors the commit while the reservation's stamped epoch still equals the bay's live epoch and the bay is currently free; a successful commit records the crane as the holder together with the epoch it committed under. The yard operator may reconfigure a bay at any time: this bumps the global epoch, re-stamps that bay with the new epoch, and clears whoever was committed on it. A crane that fell behind is slow but not failed, so it may still be holding a reservation whose stamp no longer matches the bay's epoch; such a crane drops its stale reservation. A holder may also release a bay it currently owns.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No bay slot is ever left committed to a crane under an epoch older than the bay's current reconfiguration epoch.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m8p5t4 ----
\* A pharmacy prescription dispenser uses hierarchical locks: a pharmacist must hold the coarse
\* cabinet lock before taking the fine drawer lock for a specific prescription, and must give up
\* every drawer before releasing the cabinet. Dispensing a drawer is irreversible -- it physically
\* releases a dose and moves the prescription to its terminal filled state -- and the number of
\* stocked doses is adjusted at runtime. Because a drawer can be held only under the cabinet lock,
\* two pharmacists can never both reach the irreversible dispense of the same drawer at once.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Pharmacists == {"p1", "p2"}
Scripts == {"r1", "r2"}
MaxDoses == 2

VARIABLES cabinet, holder, phase, doses

TypeOK ==
  /\ cabinet \in Pharmacists \cup {NONE}
  /\ holder \in [Scripts -> Pharmacists \cup {NONE}]
  /\ phase \in [Scripts -> {"open", "held", "done"}]
  /\ doses \in 0..MaxDoses

Init ==
  /\ cabinet = NONE
  /\ holder = [r \in Scripts |-> NONE]
  /\ phase = [r \in Scripts |-> "open"]
  /\ doses = MaxDoses

AcquireCabinet(ph) ==
  /\ cabinet = NONE
  /\ cabinet' = ph
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, phase, doses>>

AcquireDrawer(ph, r) ==
  /\ cabinet = ph
  /\ phase[r] = "open"
  /\ holder[r] = NONE
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![r] = ph]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "held"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinet, doses>>

Dispense(ph, r) ==
  /\ holder[r] = ph
  /\ phase[r] = "held"
  /\ doses > 0
  /\ doses' = doses - 1
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "done"]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED cabinet

AbortDrawer(ph, r) ==
  /\ holder[r] = ph
  /\ phase[r] = "held"
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "open"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinet, doses>>

ReleaseCabinet(ph) ==
  /\ cabinet = ph
  /\ \A r \in Scripts : holder[r] # ph
  /\ cabinet' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, phase, doses>>

Restock ==
  /\ doses < MaxDoses
  /\ doses' = doses + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinet, holder, phase>>

Next ==
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists : AcquireCabinet(ph)
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, r \in Scripts : AcquireDrawer(ph, r)
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, r \in Scripts : Dispense(ph, r)
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists, r \in Scripts : AbortDrawer(ph, r)
  \/ \E ph \in Pharmacists : ReleaseCabinet(ph)
  \/ Restock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<cabinet, holder, phase, doses>>

DrawerUnderCabinet ==
  \A r \in Scripts : holder[r] # NONE => cabinet = holder[r]
====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser guards its stock with hierarchical locks. There is one coarse cabinet lock and a fine drawer lock per prescription. A pharmacist first acquires the cabinet lock; only while holding the cabinet may the pharmacist take the fine drawer lock for a particular prescription, moving that prescription from open to held. From held the pharmacist either dispenses -- an irreversible step that consumes one stocked dose, moves the prescription to its terminal filled state, and gives up the drawer -- or aborts, returning the prescription to open. A pharmacist may release the cabinet lock only after giving up every drawer it holds. Stock is replenished at runtime, so the number of available doses changes while the system runs. Because a fine drawer can be held only under the coarse cabinet lock, at most one pharmacist can ever reach the irreversible dispense of a given drawer.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A pharmacist holds the fine drawer lock for a prescription only while also holding the coarse cabinet lock.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m4p0t2 ----
\* Two independent dispatcher instances for an elevator bank share one pool of service cars.
\* Ride requests flow through a single bounded queue with backpressure: a car may be queued only
\* while it is free and the queue is not full. Dispatching pulls the head request and takes the
\* car as a critical resource for the chosen instance; a completed run returns the car to the pool,
\* and one instance may hand a car directly to the other. Each instance keeps a private record of
\* the cars it drives, and this record stays exactly in step with the pool's ownership, so a car is
\* never driven by both instances at once.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

NONE == "none"
Instances == {"a", "b"}
Cars == {"x", "y"}
QCap == 2

VARIABLES free, owner, claim, queue

TypeOK ==
  /\ free \in SUBSET Cars
  /\ owner \in [Cars -> Instances \cup {NONE}]
  /\ claim \in [Instances -> SUBSET Cars]
  /\ queue \in Seq(Cars)

Init ==
  /\ free = Cars
  /\ owner = [c \in Cars |-> NONE]
  /\ claim = [i \in Instances |-> {}]
  /\ queue = << >>

InQueue(c) == \E k \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[k] = c

Enqueue(c) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < QCap
  /\ c \in free
  /\ ~InQueue(c)
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, c)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<free, owner, claim>>

Dispatch(i) ==
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ LET c == Head(queue) IN
       /\ c \in free
       /\ free' = free \ {c}
       /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = i]
       /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![i] = claim[i] \cup {c}]
       /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

Complete(i, c) ==
  /\ c \in claim[i]
  /\ free' = free \cup {c}
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![i] = claim[i] \ {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED queue

Handoff(i, j, c) ==
  /\ i # j
  /\ c \in claim[i]
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = j]
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![i] = claim[i] \ {c}, ![j] = claim[j] \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<free, queue>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Enqueue(c)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Dispatch(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Cars : Complete(i, c)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, j \in Instances, c \in Cars : Handoff(i, j, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<free, owner, claim, queue>>

ExclusiveDrive ==
  \A c \in Cars, i \in Instances : (c \in claim[i]) <=> (owner[c] = i)
====
nl:
An elevator bank is driven by two independent dispatcher instances that share one pool of service cars. Incoming ride requests are placed on a single bounded queue with backpressure: a car may be enqueued only when it is currently free, not already queued, and the queue is below its capacity. To dispatch, an instance takes the request at the head of the queue and seizes that car as a critical resource, removing it from the free pool, recording it as owned by that instance, and adding it to the instance's private set of driven cars. When a run completes, the car is returned to the free pool and dropped from the instance's set. One instance may also hand a car directly to the other, transferring both ownership and the private record together. The private record each instance keeps stays exactly in step with the pool's recorded owner.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A car is recorded in an instance's private driven set exactly when the pool records that same instance as the car's owner, so no car is ever driven by both instances at once.

---- MODULE W4Od3m2p2t5 ----
\* A bank's interbank settlement batch moves a unit of funds between two accounts using two-phase
\* commit. Preparing debits the source into an escrow that the coordinator holds; committing pays
\* the escrow to the destination; a normal abort or a privileged admin override returns the escrow
\* to the source. At every step the money in the two accounts plus the money parked in escrow adds
\* up to the same fixed batch total -- funds are only ever moved between the accounts and escrow,
\* never created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Accounts == {"a1", "a2"}
TOTAL == 2

VARIABLES bal, escrow, phase, deal

TypeOK ==
  /\ bal \in [Accounts -> 0..TOTAL]
  /\ escrow \in 0..TOTAL
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "prepare", "prepared"}
  /\ deal \in {NONE} \cup [src: Accounts, dst: Accounts]

Init ==
  /\ bal = [a \in Accounts |-> 1]
  /\ escrow = 0
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ deal = NONE

Propose(s, d) ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ s # d
  /\ bal[s] >= 1
  /\ deal' = [src |-> s, dst |-> d]
  /\ phase' = "prepare"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, escrow>>

Prepare ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ bal[deal.src] >= 1
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![deal.src] = bal[deal.src] - 1]
  /\ escrow' = escrow + 1
  /\ phase' = "prepared"
  /\ UNCHANGED deal

Commit ==
  /\ phase = "prepared"
  /\ escrow >= 1
  /\ escrow' = escrow - 1
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![deal.dst] = bal[deal.dst] + 1]
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ deal' = NONE

Abort ==
  /\ phase = "prepared"
  /\ escrow >= 1
  /\ escrow' = escrow - 1
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![deal.src] = bal[deal.src] + 1]
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ deal' = NONE

AdminOverride ==
  /\ phase = "prepare"
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ deal' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, escrow>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Accounts, d \in Accounts : Propose(s, d)
  \/ Prepare
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ AdminOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<bal, escrow, phase, deal>>

Conserved ==
  bal["a1"] + bal["a2"] + escrow = TOTAL
====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch transfers one unit of funds between two accounts using two-phase commit. A proposal picks a source and a destination while the coordinator is idle and the source is funded. Preparing debits one unit from the source into an escrow that the coordinator holds, moving to the prepared state. Committing pays the escrowed unit to the destination and returns to idle. A normal abort from the prepared state returns the escrowed unit to the source. A privileged admin override can cancel a proposal that has not yet prepared, before any funds have moved. At every step, the funds held in the two accounts together with the funds parked in escrow sum to the same fixed batch total.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The balances of the two accounts plus the amount held in escrow always equal the fixed batch total, so no funds are ever created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od1m1p1t2 ----
\* An air-traffic runway allocator keeps one shared schedule record that two controller instances
\* update through a circulating token. A controller first reads the record's version; it may commit
\* a write only while it holds the token and its read version still matches the live version, which
\* then advances by one and appends the base version it built on to the write log. A controller
\* whose read has gone stale abandons it and must read again. Because every committed write builds
\* on the version immediately before it, the log of base versions is a gap-free chain 0,1,2,... and
\* no update is silently lost by overwriting a concurrent one.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Controllers == {"c1", "c2"}
MaxVer == 2

VARIABLES version, wlog, token, staged, reading

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ wlog \in Seq(0..MaxVer)
  /\ token \in Controllers
  /\ staged \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ reading \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ wlog = << >>
  /\ token = "c1"
  /\ staged = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ reading = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]

Read(c) ==
  /\ ~reading[c]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = version]
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, wlog, token>>

PassToken(c) ==
  /\ token = c
  /\ token' = CHOOSE d \in Controllers : d # c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, wlog, staged, reading>>

Write(c) ==
  /\ token = c
  /\ reading[c]
  /\ staged[c] = version
  /\ version < MaxVer
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ wlog' = Append(wlog, version)
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, staged>>

Retry(c) ==
  /\ reading[c]
  /\ staged[c] # version
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, wlog, token, staged>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Read(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : PassToken(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Write(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Retry(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<version, wlog, token, staged, reading>>

ContiguousLog ==
  \A k \in 1..Len(wlog) : wlog[k] = k - 1
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator maintains one shared schedule record with a version number, updated by two controller instances that pass a single token around a ring. A controller reads the record, staging the version it saw. Only the controller currently holding the token may commit a write, and only if its staged version still equals the live version; the write advances the version by one and appends the base version it built upon to a write log. A controller may pass the token to the other. If a controller's staged read no longer matches the live version, it abandons the read and must read again before writing. Every committed write therefore builds on the version immediately preceding it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The log of base versions on which committed writes were built is a gap-free chain 0,1,2,..., so no update overwrites a concurrent one and no update is lost.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m4p3t2 ----
\* An airport baggage router assigns bags to chutes drawn from one shared pool, driven by two router
\* instances. Routing tasks flow through a bounded queue with backpressure. Routing a bag places it
\* into a free chute, recording both the bag's chute and the chute's bag; a bag may be rerouted to
\* another free chute, and unloading clears a chute. The bag-to-chute and chute-to-bag records are
\* kept as exact inverses of each other, so a bag occupies exactly one chute and a chute holds
\* exactly one bag -- the same chute is never allocated to two bags at once.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

NONE == "none"
Bags == {"b1", "b2"}
Chutes == {"h1", "h2"}
Instances == {"a", "b"}
QCap == 2

VARIABLES bagChute, chuteBag, queue, routedBy

TypeOK ==
  /\ bagChute \in [Bags -> Chutes \cup {NONE}]
  /\ chuteBag \in [Chutes -> Bags \cup {NONE}]
  /\ queue \in Seq(Bags)
  /\ routedBy \in [Bags -> Instances \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ bagChute = [b \in Bags |-> NONE]
  /\ chuteBag = [h \in Chutes |-> NONE]
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ routedBy = [b \in Bags |-> NONE]

InQueue(b) == \E k \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[k] = b

Enqueue(b) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < QCap
  /\ bagChute[b] = NONE
  /\ ~InQueue(b)
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bagChute, chuteBag, routedBy>>

Route(i, h) ==
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ LET b == Head(queue) IN
       /\ bagChute[b] = NONE
       /\ chuteBag[h] = NONE
       /\ bagChute' = [bagChute EXCEPT ![b] = h]
       /\ chuteBag' = [chuteBag EXCEPT ![h] = b]
       /\ routedBy' = [routedBy EXCEPT ![b] = i]
       /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

Reroute(i, b, h) ==
  /\ bagChute[b] # NONE
  /\ bagChute[b] # h
  /\ chuteBag[h] = NONE
  /\ chuteBag' = [chuteBag EXCEPT ![bagChute[b]] = NONE, ![h] = b]
  /\ bagChute' = [bagChute EXCEPT ![b] = h]
  /\ routedBy' = [routedBy EXCEPT ![b] = i]
  /\ UNCHANGED queue

Unload(h) ==
  /\ chuteBag[h] # NONE
  /\ LET b == chuteBag[h] IN
       /\ bagChute' = [bagChute EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
       /\ chuteBag' = [chuteBag EXCEPT ![h] = NONE]
       /\ routedBy' = [routedBy EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
       /\ UNCHANGED queue

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Enqueue(b)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, h \in Chutes : Route(i, h)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Bags, h \in Chutes : Reroute(i, b, h)
  \/ \E h \in Chutes : Unload(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<bagChute, chuteBag, queue, routedBy>>

InverseMaps ==
  \A b \in Bags, h \in Chutes : (bagChute[b] = h) <=> (chuteBag[h] = b)
====
nl:
An airport baggage router assigns bags to chutes drawn from one shared pool, worked by two router instances. Routing tasks pass through a single bounded queue with backpressure, where a bag may be queued only while unrouted, not already queued, and the queue has room. Routing takes the head bag and places it into a free chute, recording both the bag's chute and the chute's bag. A bag may be rerouted to another free chute, atomically clearing its old chute and occupying the new one. Unloading clears a chute and its bag. The bag-to-chute map and the chute-to-bag map are maintained as exact inverses of each other at all times.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bag occupies a chute exactly when that chute holds that bag, so the same chute is never allocated to two bags at once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m4p6t0 ----
\* A smart-home door-lock network processes lock and unlock commands through a bounded queue with
\* backpressure. Only a currently enrolled device may enqueue or run a command, and one device may
\* crash silently, after which it issues nothing more. Running a command latches the door and records
\* which device actuated it. Revoking a device drops it from the enrolled set and immediately clears
\* any door it had latched, and a command from a no-longer-enrolled device is discarded rather than
\* run. Thus every door that is latched was actuated by a device that is still enrolled -- no stale
\* or unauthorized participant leaves a standing effect.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

NONE == "none"
Devices == {"d1", "d2"}
Doors == {"g1"}
QCap == 2
Cmds == {"lock", "unlock"}

VARIABLES enrolled, crashed, queue, actor, latch

Msg == [dev: Devices, door: Doors, cmd: Cmds]

TypeOK ==
  /\ enrolled \in SUBSET Devices
  /\ crashed \in SUBSET Devices
  /\ queue \in Seq(Msg)
  /\ actor \in [Doors -> Devices \cup {NONE}]
  /\ latch \in [Doors -> Cmds \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ enrolled = Devices
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ actor = [g \in Doors |-> NONE]
  /\ latch = [g \in Doors |-> NONE]

Enqueue(d, g, k) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < QCap
  /\ d \in enrolled
  /\ d \notin crashed
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, [dev |-> d, door |-> g, cmd |-> k])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, crashed, actor, latch>>

Run ==
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ LET m == Head(queue) IN
       /\ m.dev \in enrolled
       /\ m.dev \notin crashed
       /\ actor' = [actor EXCEPT ![m.door] = m.dev]
       /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![m.door] = m.cmd]
       /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
       /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, crashed>>

Discard ==
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ Head(queue).dev \notin enrolled
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, crashed, actor, latch>>

Revoke(d) ==
  /\ d \in enrolled
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled \ {d}
  /\ actor' = [g \in Doors |-> IF actor[g] = d THEN NONE ELSE actor[g]]
  /\ latch' = [g \in Doors |-> IF actor[g] = d THEN NONE ELSE latch[g]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, queue>>

Enroll(d) ==
  /\ d \notin enrolled
  /\ d \notin crashed
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, queue, actor, latch>>

Crash(d) ==
  /\ d \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, queue, actor, latch>>

Recover(d) ==
  /\ d \in crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \ {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, queue, actor, latch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Devices, g \in Doors, k \in Cmds : Enqueue(d, g, k)
  \/ Run
  \/ Discard
  \/ \E d \in Devices : Revoke(d)
  \/ \E d \in Devices : Enroll(d)
  \/ \E d \in Devices : Crash(d)
  \/ \E d \in Devices : Recover(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<enrolled, crashed, queue, actor, latch>>

LatchedByEnrolled ==
  \A g \in Doors : actor[g] # NONE => actor[g] \in enrolled
====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network runs lock and unlock commands through a single bounded queue with backpressure. Each command names the issuing device, a door, and the action. Only a currently enrolled, non-crashed device may enqueue a command, and only such a device's command at the head of the queue is run, latching the door and recording the actuating device. A device may crash silently, after which it issues nothing further. An operator may revoke a device, removing it from the enrolled set and immediately clearing any door that device had latched; a device may also be re-enrolled. A queued command whose issuer is no longer enrolled is discarded rather than run.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every door that is currently latched was actuated by a device that is still enrolled, so no unauthorized or revoked device leaves a standing effect.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m9p6t1 ----
\* A pharmacy prescription dispenser is driven by epoch-numbered reconfiguration and receives
\* command messages that may be reordered, modeled as an unordered pool. Each message carries the
\* device that issued it and the epoch it was issued under. The dispenser runs a message only while
\* the message's epoch equals the live epoch and its issuer is currently authorized, recording that

\* clears the recorded server. Stale messages from an old epoch are dropped. So whenever a server is
\* recorded it acted under the current epoch -- no stale-epoch command ever stands.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Devices == {"d1", "d2"}
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, authz, inbox, server, servEpoch

  /\ authz \in SUBSET Devices

  /\ m.ep = epoch
  /\ m.dev \in authz
  /\ server' = m.dev
  /\ servEpoch' = epoch
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}

Drop(m) ==
  /\ m \in inbox
  /\ m.ep # epoch
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}

Next ==

  \/ \E na \in SUBSET Devices : Reconfig(na)

A pharmacy prescription dispenser is governed by epoch-numbered reconfiguration and receives command messages that may arrive reordered, modeled as an unordered pool. ---- MODULE W4Od12m6p3t2 ----
\* A blood-bank inventory tracker leases units from one shared pool to two tracker instances using
\* time-limited leases modeled as a remaining time-to-live. An instance first reserves a free unit,
\* then acquires it, which grants ownership and charges the lease to its full span. The owner may
\* renew the lease back to full span, or release the unit early. As the lease decays, its remaining
\* time drops by one each step, and the instant it would reach zero the unit is reclaimed to the free
\* pool with its owner cleared. So any unit still recorded as owned has strictly positive remaining
\* lease time -- an unexpired unit is never handed out a second time while an owner still holds it.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Units == {"u1", "u2"}
Instances == {"a", "b"}
Span == 2

VARIABLES owner, ttl, pool, request

TypeOK ==
  /\ owner \in [Units -> Instances \cup {NONE}]
  /\ ttl \in [Units -> 0..Span]
  /\ pool \in SUBSET Units
  /\ request \in [Units -> Instances \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ owner = [u \in Units |-> NONE]
  /\ ttl = [u \in Units |-> 0]
  /\ pool = Units
  /\ request = [u \in Units |-> NONE]

Reserve(i, u) ==
  /\ u \in pool
  /\ request[u] = NONE
  /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![u] = i]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ttl, pool>>

Acquire(i, u) ==
  /\ u \in pool
  /\ request[u] = i
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![u] = i]
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![u] = Span]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {u}
  /\ request' = [request EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]

Renew(i, u) ==
  /\ owner[u] = i
  /\ ttl[u] > 0
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![u] = Span]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, pool, request>>

Release(i, u) ==
  /\ owner[u] = i
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![u] = 0]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED request

Decay(u) ==
  /\ owner[u] # NONE
  /\ ttl[u] > 1
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![u] = ttl[u] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, pool, request>>

Lapse(u) ==
  /\ owner[u] # NONE
  /\ ttl[u] = 1
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![u] = 0]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED request

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances, u \in Units : Reserve(i, u)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, u \in Units : Acquire(i, u)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, u \in Units : Renew(i, u)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, u \in Units : Release(i, u)
  \/ \E u \in Units : Decay(u)
  \/ \E u \in Units : Lapse(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<owner, ttl, pool, request>>

PoolCoherent ==
  \A u \in Units : (u \in pool) <=> (owner[u] = NONE)

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker leases units from one shared pool to two tracker instances using time-limited leases. Acquiring a free unit assigns it to an instance and stamps it with an expiry a fixed span into the future; the owning instance may renew the lease before it lapses, or release the unit early back to the pool. A clock tick advances the current time and, in the same atomic step, reclaims every unit whose lease has lapsed, returning it to the free pool and clearing its owner. Because a lapsed lease is always reclaimed as time advances, a unit recorded as owned always has an expiry strictly after the current time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A unit sits in the free pool exactly when it has no owner, so a unit currently owned under a live lease is never simultaneously available to be allocated a second time.

---- MODULE W4Od5m8p1t5 ----
\* A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker protects lobby rosters with hierarchical locks: a matchmaker
\* takes the coarse region lock before any fine per-lobby lock, and updates a lobby's roster version
\* only while holding that lobby's fine lock. It must drop every fine lock before releasing the coarse
\* lock. A privileged admin override may forcibly drop all locks at once. Because a fine lobby lock is
\* only ever held by the matchmaker that also holds the coarse region lock, two matchmakers can never
\* be writing the same lobby at once, so no roster update is silently lost to a concurrent write.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Matchmakers == {"m1", "m2"}
Lobbies == {"L1", "L2"}
MaxVer == 2

VARIABLES coarse, fine, version, lastWriter

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Matchmakers \cup {NONE}
  /\ fine \in [Lobbies -> Matchmakers \cup {NONE}]
  /\ version \in [Lobbies -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ lastWriter \in [Lobbies -> Matchmakers \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ fine = [l \in Lobbies |-> NONE]
  /\ version = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]
  /\ lastWriter = [l \in Lobbies |-> NONE]

AcquireCoarse(m) ==
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ coarse' = m
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, version, lastWriter>>

AcquireFine(m, l) ==
  /\ coarse = m
  /\ fine[l] = NONE
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![l] = m]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, version, lastWriter>>

Write(m, l) ==
  /\ fine[l] = m
  /\ version[l] < MaxVer
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![l] = version[l] + 1]
  /\ lastWriter' = [lastWriter EXCEPT ![l] = m]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

ReleaseFine(m, l) ==
  /\ fine[l] = m
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![l] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, version, lastWriter>>

ReleaseCoarse(m) ==
  /\ coarse = m
  /\ \A l \in Lobbies : fine[l] # m
  /\ coarse' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, version, lastWriter>>

AdminOverride ==
  /\ coarse # NONE \/ \E l \in Lobbies : fine[l] # NONE
  /\ coarse' = NONE
  /\ fine' = [l \in Lobbies |-> NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, lastWriter>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Matchmakers : AcquireCoarse(m)
  \/ \E m \in Matchmakers, l \in Lobbies : AcquireFine(m, l)
  \/ \E m \in Matchmakers, l \in Lobbies : Write(m, l)
  \/ \E m \in Matchmakers, l \in Lobbies : ReleaseFine(m, l)
  \/ \E m \in Matchmakers : ReleaseCoarse(m)
  \/ AdminOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, fine, version, lastWriter>>

LockNesting ==
  \A l \in Lobbies : fine[l] # NONE => coarse = fine[l]
====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker protects lobby rosters with hierarchical locks. There is one coarse region lock and one fine lock per lobby. A matchmaker must acquire the coarse region lock before taking any fine lobby lock. Only while holding a lobby's fine lock may the matchmaker write that lobby, advancing its roster version and recording itself as the last writer. A matchmaker must release every fine lock it holds before it may release the coarse lock. A privileged admin override may forcibly drop the coarse lock and all fine locks in a single step. A fine lobby lock is therefore only ever held by the matchmaker that also holds the coarse region lock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A matchmaker holds a lobby's fine lock only while it also holds the coarse region lock, so two matchmakers never write the same lobby's roster concurrently and no update is lost.

---- MODULE W4Od18m6p3t4 ----
\* A smart-home door-lock network leases exclusive control of doors to users under time-limited
\* leases, with the number of concurrently grantable leases (the capacity) changing at runtime.
\* A grant is admitted only while the user and door are both free and the active-lease count is under
\* the current capacity; it records the door on the user and the user on the door as exact inverses.
\* A lease may be renewed, released, or allowed to lapse as its remaining time decays to zero. The
\* user-to-door and door-to-user records stay mutual inverses, so a door under a live lease is never
\* granted to a second user.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

NONE == "none"
Users == {"u1", "u2"}
Doors == {"g1", "g2"}
MaxCap == 2
Span == 2

VARIABLES holds, doorUser, lease, capacity

TypeOK ==
  /\ holds \in [Users -> Doors \cup {NONE}]
  /\ doorUser \in [Doors -> Users \cup {NONE}]
  /\ lease \in [Doors -> 0..Span]
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
  /\ holds = [u \in Users |-> NONE]
  /\ doorUser = [g \in Doors |-> NONE]
  /\ lease = [g \in Doors |-> 0]
  /\ capacity = 1

Active == Cardinality({g \in Doors : doorUser[g] # NONE})

AdjustCapacity(c) ==
  /\ capacity' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, doorUser, lease>>

Grant(u, g) ==
  /\ holds[u] = NONE
  /\ doorUser[g] = NONE
  /\ Active < capacity
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![u] = g]
  /\ doorUser' = [doorUser EXCEPT ![g] = u]
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![g] = Span]
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Renew(u, g) ==
  /\ doorUser[g] = u
  /\ lease[g] > 0
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![g] = Span]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, doorUser, capacity>>

Release(u, g) ==
  /\ doorUser[g] = u
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]
  /\ doorUser' = [doorUser EXCEPT ![g] = NONE]
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![g] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Decay(g) ==
  /\ doorUser[g] # NONE
  /\ lease[g] > 1
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![g] = lease[g] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, doorUser, capacity>>

Lapse(g) ==
  /\ doorUser[g] # NONE
  /\ lease[g] = 1
  /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![doorUser[g]] = NONE]
  /\ doorUser' = [doorUser EXCEPT ![g] = NONE]
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![g] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in 0..MaxCap : AdjustCapacity(c)
  \/ \E u \in Users, g \in Doors : Grant(u, g)
  \/ \E u \in Users, g \in Doors : Renew(u, g)
  \/ \E u \in Users, g \in Doors : Release(u, g)
  \/ \E g \in Doors : Decay(g)
  \/ \E g \in Doors : Lapse(g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<holds, doorUser, lease, capacity>>

InverseHold ==
  \A u \in Users, g \in Doors : (holds[u] = g) <=> (doorUser[g] = u)
====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network grants exclusive control of doors to users under time-limited leases, and the capacity -- the number of leases that may be active at once -- is adjusted at runtime. A grant is admitted only when the chosen user and door are both currently free and the number of active leases is below the current capacity; it records the door on the user and the user on the door, and charges the lease to its full span. A lease may be renewed to full span, released early, or left to decay one step at a time until it lapses and is cleared. The user-to-door and door-to-user records are kept as exact inverses of one another.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A user records a door exactly when that door records that user, so a door under a live lease is never allocated to a second user.

---- MODULE W4Od6m7p1t1 ----
\* An elevator bank keeps a shared control register (a value plus a version) that instances update
\* through compare-and-swap. Proposals may arrive reordered, modeled as an unordered pool: each names
\* an expected version and a new value. A compare-and-swap succeeds only when its expected version
\* equals the live version, whereupon it stores the new value, advances the version, and appends the
\* value to the commit history; a proposal whose expected version is stale is dropped without effect.
\* A maintenance write may also post a value directly, advancing register and history together. The
\* register always equals the most recently committed value, so no update is lost by a blind overwrite.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

MaxVer == 2
Vals == {0, 1}

VARIABLES reg, version, hist, inbox

Prop == [exp: 0..MaxVer, val: Vals]

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in Vals
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ hist \in Seq(Vals)
  /\ inbox \in SUBSET Prop

Init ==
  /\ reg = 0
  /\ version = 0
  /\ hist = << >>
  /\ inbox = {}

Propose(e, v) ==
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[exp |-> e, val |-> v]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, version, hist>>

CAS(p) ==
  /\ p \in inbox
  /\ p.exp = version
  /\ version < MaxVer
  /\ reg' = p.val
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ hist' = Append(hist, p.val)
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {p}

Fail(p) ==
  /\ p \in inbox
  /\ p.exp # version
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, version, hist>>

MaintWrite(v) ==
  /\ version < MaxVer
  /\ reg' = v
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ hist' = Append(hist, v)
  /\ UNCHANGED inbox

Next ==
  \/ \E e \in 0..MaxVer, v \in Vals : Propose(e, v)
  \/ \E p \in inbox : CAS(p)
  \/ \E p \in inbox : Fail(p)
  \/ \E v \in Vals : MaintWrite(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, version, hist, inbox>>

RegMatchesHistory ==
  IF hist = << >> THEN reg = 0 ELSE reg = hist[Len(hist)]
====
nl:
An elevator bank maintains one shared control register holding a value and a version, updated by instances through compare-and-swap. Proposals may arrive reordered and are held in an unordered pool; each proposal names an expected version and a new value. A compare-and-swap succeeds only when its expected version matches the live version, at which point it stores the new value, advances the version by one, and appends the value to the commit history. A proposal whose expected version no longer matches is dropped with no effect. A maintenance write may also post a value directly, advancing the register, version, and history together.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The register always equals the most recently committed value in the history, so no update is lost by a blind overwrite of a concurrent one.

---- MODULE W4Od16m9p0t2 ----
\* A pharmacy prescription dispenser exposes one critical dispensing station shared by two dispenser
\* instances, coordinated by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. An instance observes the live epoch, and
\* may seize the free station only while its observed epoch is current, taking the station and setting
\* its own belief that it holds it. Releasing frees the station and clears the belief. A reconfiguration
\* bumps the epoch, frees the station, and clears every instance's belief. Each instance believes it
\* holds the station exactly when it is the recorded holder, so the two instances never both occupy the
\* critical station at once.

NONE == "none"
Instances == {"a", "b"}
MaxEpoch == 2

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ holder \in Instances \cup {NONE}
  /\ believes \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ seenEpoch \in [Instances -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ holder = NONE
  /\ believes = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ seenEpoch = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

Observe(i) ==
  /\ seenEpoch' = [seenEpoch EXCEPT ![i] = epoch]

Acquire(i) ==

ReleaseStation(i) ==

  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]

Reconfig ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ holder' = NONE
  /\ believes' = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED seenEpoch

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Observe(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Acquire(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : ReleaseStation(i)

  \A i \in Instances : believes[i] <=> (holder = i)

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser has one critical dispensing station shared by two dispenser instances, coordinated by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. An instance observes the current epoch, recording the epoch it saw. It may seize the station only while the station is free and its observed epoch still equals the live epoch; seizing records it as the station's holder and sets its own belief that it holds the station. Releasing frees the station and clears that belief. A reconfiguration bumps the epoch, frees the station, and clears every instance's belief so stale holders cannot linger.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p0t2 ----
\* A bank's interbank settlement batch is driven by a single elected leader among two nodes that share
\* one settlement pool, with leader election and failover across terms. Starting a new term clears the
\* leader and every vote. Each node casts one vote per term; a node is elected leader only once both
\* nodes have voted for it, giving it the whole quorum. The leader advances the settlement batch. On
\* failover the leader crashes and is cleared, and stalled votes may be cleared to retry. Whenever a
\* leader stands, every node's current vote names that leader, so at most one node ever leads a term.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Nodes == {"n1", "n2"}
MaxTerm == 2
MaxBatch == 2

VARIABLES term, leader, votedFor, batch

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
  /\ votedFor \in [Nodes -> Nodes \cup {NONE}]
  /\ batch \in 0..MaxBatch

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ votedFor = [n \in Nodes |-> NONE]
  /\ batch = 0

StartTerm ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ leader' = NONE
  /\ votedFor' = [n \in Nodes |-> NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED batch

Vote(n, cand) ==
  /\ votedFor[n] = NONE
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![n] = cand]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, batch>>

Elect(cand) ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ \A n \in Nodes : votedFor[n] = cand
  /\ leader' = cand
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, votedFor, batch>>

Settle(n) ==
  /\ leader = n
  /\ batch < MaxBatch
  /\ batch' = batch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, votedFor>>

Crash(n) ==
  /\ leader = n
  /\ leader' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, votedFor, batch>>

ClearVotes ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ \E n \in Nodes : votedFor[n] # NONE
  /\ votedFor' = [n \in Nodes |-> NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, batch>>

Next ==
  \/ StartTerm
  \/ \E n \in Nodes, cand \in Nodes : Vote(n, cand)
  \/ \E cand \in Nodes : Elect(cand)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Settle(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
  \/ ClearVotes

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<term, leader, votedFor, batch>>

LeaderBacked ==
  leader # NONE => \A n \in Nodes : votedFor[n] = leader
====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is driven by a single elected leader chosen from two nodes that share one settlement pool, using leader election with failover across terms. Starting a new term increments the term and clears the leader and all votes. Each node casts one vote per term for a candidate while there is no leader. A candidate is elected leader only once every node has voted for it, giving it the full quorum. The leader advances the shared settlement batch. On failover the current leader crashes and is cleared; when an election stalls without a leader, the votes may be cleared so the nodes can vote again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a leader stands, every node's current vote names that leader, so at most one node ever leads a given term.

---- MODULE W4Od15m5p0t3 ----
\* A stock exchange opening auction clears at a price agreed by quorum voting across three matching
\* replicas. In each round every replica casts one vote for a candidate clearing price; a replica may
\* be slow but not failed, so it can vote late while the others proceed. A price is chosen only once a
\* strict majority of replicas have voted for it, after which the chosen match fills the auction book.
\* An idle result may be dissolved and a fresh round started, clearing all votes. Whenever a price is
\* chosen it is backed by a quorum of votes, so two different prices can never both be chosen.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

NONE == "none"
Replicas == {"r1", "r2", "r3"}
Prices == {"p1", "p2"}
Quorum == 2
MaxRound == 2
MaxBook == 2

VARIABLES voted, chosen, round, book

TypeOK ==
  /\ voted \in [Replicas -> Prices \cup {NONE}]
  /\ chosen \in Prices \cup {NONE}
  /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
  /\ book \in 0..MaxBook

Init ==
  /\ voted = [r \in Replicas |-> NONE]
  /\ chosen = NONE
  /\ round = 0
  /\ book = 0

Support(p) == Cardinality({r \in Replicas : voted[r] = p})

CastVote(r, p) ==
  /\ voted[r] = NONE
  /\ chosen = NONE
  /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![r] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chosen, round, book>>

Choose(p) ==
  /\ chosen = NONE
  /\ Support(p) >= Quorum
  /\ chosen' = p
  /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, round, book>>

Fill ==
  /\ chosen # NONE
  /\ book < MaxBook
  /\ book' = book + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, chosen, round>>

NextRound ==
  /\ chosen # NONE
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ voted' = [r \in Replicas |-> NONE]
  /\ chosen' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED book

Dissolve ==
  /\ chosen # NONE
  /\ chosen' = NONE
  /\ voted' = [r \in Replicas |-> NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, book>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Replicas, p \in Prices : CastVote(r, p)
  \/ \E p \in Prices : Choose(p)
  \/ Fill
  \/ NextRound
  \/ Dissolve

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<voted, chosen, round, book>>

ChosenHasQuorum ==
  chosen # NONE => Support(chosen) >= Quorum
====
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction clears at a price agreed by quorum voting across three matching replicas. In each round, every replica casts one vote for a candidate clearing price while no price is yet chosen; a replica may be slow but not failed, so it can vote late while the others proceed. A price is chosen only once a strict majority of the replicas have voted for it. Once a price is chosen, the resulting match fills the auction book. A chosen result may be dissolved, clearing all votes, and a fresh round may be started, which also clears all votes and advances the round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a price is chosen, it is backed by at least a quorum of replica votes, so two different prices can never both be chosen.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m8p1t4 ----
\* A smart-home door-lock network maintains one shared usage counter that two writers increment under
\* hierarchical locks: a writer takes the coarse hub lock before the fine counter lock, and only under
\* the fine lock may it increment, bumping both the shared counter and its own recorded contribution.
\* The counter's ceiling (capacity) is adjusted at runtime, and increments are admitted only below it.
\* Every writer must drop the fine lock before releasing the coarse lock. The shared counter always
\* equals the sum of the writers' recorded contributions, so no increment is ever lost or double-counted.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Writers == {"w1", "w2"}
MaxTotal == 3

VARIABLES coarse, fine, total, contrib, capacity

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Writers \cup {NONE}
  /\ fine \in Writers \cup {NONE}
  /\ total \in 0..MaxTotal
  /\ contrib \in [Writers -> 0..MaxTotal]
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxTotal

Init ==
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ fine = NONE
  /\ total = 0
  /\ contrib = [w \in Writers |-> 0]
  /\ capacity = 2

AcquireCoarse(w) ==
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ coarse' = w
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, total, contrib, capacity>>

AcquireFine(w) ==
  /\ coarse = w
  /\ fine = NONE
  /\ fine' = w
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, total, contrib, capacity>>

Increment(w) ==
  /\ fine = w
  /\ total < capacity
  /\ total < MaxTotal
  /\ total' = total + 1
  /\ contrib' = [contrib EXCEPT ![w] = contrib[w] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, capacity>>

ReleaseFine(w) ==
  /\ fine = w
  /\ fine' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, total, contrib, capacity>>

ReleaseCoarse(w) ==
  /\ coarse = w
  /\ fine # w
  /\ coarse' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, total, contrib, capacity>>

AdjustCapacity(c) ==
  /\ capacity' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, total, contrib>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Writers : AcquireCoarse(w)
  \/ \E w \in Writers : AcquireFine(w)
  \/ \E w \in Writers : Increment(w)
  \/ \E w \in Writers : ReleaseFine(w)
  \/ \E w \in Writers : ReleaseCoarse(w)
  \/ \E c \in 0..MaxTotal : AdjustCapacity(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, fine, total, contrib, capacity>>

TotalMatchesContribs ==
  total = contrib["w1"] + contrib["w2"]
====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network maintains one shared usage counter that two writers increment under hierarchical locks. A writer must acquire the coarse hub lock before the fine counter lock, and only while holding the fine lock may it increment the counter, which bumps both the shared total and that writer's own recorded contribution. The counter's ceiling, its capacity, is adjusted at runtime, and an increment is admitted only while the total is below the current capacity. A writer must drop the fine lock before releasing the coarse lock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared counter always equals the sum of the two writers' recorded contributions, so no increment is ever lost or double-counted.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p3t5 ----
\* A subway signalling block system routes trains onto track blocks through a bounded request queue
\* with backpressure. A block's signal shows green when free and red when occupied. Allocating pulls
\* a queued request and, only if the target block's signal is green, moves the train onto it, turning
\* the signal red and recording the train's position. Releasing frees the block, greening its signal.
\* A privileged admin override may force-clear a block. A block's signal is red exactly when a train
\* occupies it, so a green block is only ever allocated to one train -- the same block is never
\* double-allocated.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

NONE == "none"
Trains == {"t1", "t2"}
Blocks == {"b1", "b2"}
QCap == 2

VARIABLES occupied, signal, queue, at

Req == [train: Trains, block: Blocks]

TypeOK ==
  /\ occupied \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {NONE}]
  /\ signal \in [Blocks -> {"green", "red"}]
  /\ queue \in Seq(Req)
  /\ at \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ occupied = [b \in Blocks |-> NONE]
  /\ signal = [b \in Blocks |-> "green"]
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ at = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]

Queued(t, b) == \E k \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[k] = [train |-> t, block |-> b]

Request(t, b) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < QCap
  /\ ~Queued(t, b)
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, [train |-> t, block |-> b])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupied, signal, at>>

Allocate ==
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ LET rq == Head(queue) IN
       /\ signal[rq.block] = "green"
       /\ at[rq.train] = NONE
       /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![rq.block] = rq.train]
       /\ signal' = [signal EXCEPT ![rq.block] = "red"]
       /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![rq.train] = rq.block]
       /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

Release(t, b) ==
  /\ occupied[b] = t
  /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
  /\ signal' = [signal EXCEPT ![b] = "green"]
  /\ at' = [at EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED queue

AdminClear(b) ==
  /\ occupied[b] # NONE
  /\ occupied' = [occupied EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
  /\ signal' = [signal EXCEPT ![b] = "green"]
  /\ at' = [t \in Trains |-> IF at[t] = b THEN NONE ELSE at[t]]
  /\ UNCHANGED queue

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Request(t, b)
  \/ Allocate
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Release(t, b)
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : AdminClear(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<occupied, signal, queue, at>>

SignalCoherent ==
  \A b \in Blocks : (occupied[b] # NONE) <=> (signal[b] = "red")
====
nl:
A subway signalling block system routes trains onto track blocks through a bounded request queue with backpressure. Each block's signal shows green when the block is free and red when a train occupies it. A request naming a train and a target block is queued while the queue has room and that request is not already present. Allocating takes the request at the head of the queue and, only if the target block's signal is green and the train is not already on a block, moves the train onto the block, turns the signal red, and records the train's position. Releasing frees a block and turns its signal green. A privileged admin override may force-clear an occupied block, greening its signal and clearing any train recorded there.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A block's signal is red exactly when a train occupies that block, so a green block is only ever allocated to a single train and no block is double-allocated.

---- MODULE W4Od0m4p1t1 ----
\* A hospital operating-room scheduler applies edits to shared booking records through a bounded
\* intake queue with backpressure; edits may be delivered reordered, so the queue is an unordered
\* pool capped in size. Each edit names a record, the base version it was built on, and a new value.
\* An edit is applied only when its base version matches that record's live version, whereupon the
\* record takes the new value, advances its version, and appends the value to that record's commit
\* history; a stale edit is discarded. A supervisor may also amend a record directly. Each record's
\* stored value always equals the last value in its own commit history, so no edit is silently lost.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

Records == {"r1", "r2"}
MaxVer == 2
Vals == {0, 1}
QCap == 2

VARIABLES value, version, hist, inbox

Edit == [rec: Records, base: 0..MaxVer, val: Vals]

TypeOK ==
  /\ value \in [Records -> Vals]
  /\ version \in [Records -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ hist \in [Records -> Seq(Vals)]
  /\ inbox \in SUBSET Edit

Init ==
  /\ value = [r \in Records |-> 0]
  /\ version = [r \in Records |-> 0]
  /\ hist = [r \in Records |-> << >>]
  /\ inbox = {}

Submit(r, b, v) ==
  /\ Cardinality(inbox) < QCap
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[rec |-> r, base |-> b, val |-> v]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, hist>>

Apply(e) ==
  /\ e \in inbox
  /\ e.base = version[e.rec]
  /\ version[e.rec] < MaxVer
  /\ value' = [value EXCEPT ![e.rec] = e.val]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![e.rec] = version[e.rec] + 1]
  /\ hist' = [hist EXCEPT ![e.rec] = Append(hist[e.rec], e.val)]
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {e}

Reject(e) ==
  /\ e \in inbox
  /\ (e.base # version[e.rec] \/ version[e.rec] = MaxVer)
  /\ inbox' = inbox \ {e}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, hist>>

Amend(r, v) ==
  /\ version[r] < MaxVer
  /\ value' = [value EXCEPT ![r] = v]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![r] = version[r] + 1]
  /\ hist' = [hist EXCEPT ![r] = Append(hist[r], v)]
  /\ UNCHANGED inbox

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Records, b \in 0..MaxVer, v \in Vals : Submit(r, b, v)
  \/ \E e \in inbox : Apply(e)
  \/ \E e \in inbox : Reject(e)
  \/ \E r \in Records, v \in Vals : Amend(r, v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<value, version, hist, inbox>>

ValueMatchesLog ==
  \A r \in Records :
    IF hist[r] = << >> THEN value[r] = 0 ELSE value[r] = hist[r][Len(hist[r])]
====
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler applies edits to shared booking records through a bounded intake queue with backpressure. Edits may be delivered reordered, so the queue is an unordered pool capped in size. Each edit names a record, the base version it was built upon, and a new value. Submitting adds an edit to the pool while the pool is below its cap. An edit is applied only when its base version matches that record's live version, at which point the record takes the new value, advances its version by one, and appends the value to that record's commit history. An edit whose base version is stale is discarded unused. A supervisor may amend a record directly, advancing its value, version, and history together.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Each record's stored value always equals the last value recorded in that record's own commit history, so no concurrent edit is silently lost.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m0p0t3 ----
\* A bank's interbank settlement batch guards one critical ledger section with optimistic locking.
\* A worker reads the current generation counter into its staged view; a worker may be slow but not
\* failed, so its staged view can lag behind. A worker enters the critical section only when the
\* section is free and its staged view still equals the live generation, at which point it records
\* the entry generation and bumps the generation. Inside, it advances the settlement batch; leaving
\* bumps the generation again. Whenever a worker occupies the section, the live generation is exactly
\* one past the generation it entered on, so no second worker is ever inside at the same time.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Workers == {"w1", "w2"}
MaxGen == 3
MaxBatch == 2

VARIABLES gen, occupant, entryGen, staged, batch

TypeOK ==
  /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
  /\ occupant \in Workers \cup {NONE}
  /\ entryGen \in 0..MaxGen
  /\ staged \in [Workers -> 0..MaxGen]
  /\ batch \in 0..MaxBatch

Init ==
  /\ gen = 0
  /\ occupant = NONE
  /\ entryGen = 0
  /\ staged = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ batch = 0

Read(w) ==
  /\ staged[w] # gen
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![w] = gen]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, occupant, entryGen, batch>>

Enter(w) ==
  /\ occupant = NONE
  /\ staged[w] = gen
  /\ gen < MaxGen
  /\ occupant' = w
  /\ entryGen' = gen
  /\ gen' = gen + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, batch>>

Work(w) ==
  /\ occupant = w
  /\ batch < MaxBatch
  /\ batch' = batch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, occupant, entryGen, staged>>

Leave(w) ==
  /\ occupant = w
  /\ occupant' = NONE
  /\ gen' = IF gen < MaxGen THEN gen + 1 ELSE gen
  /\ UNCHANGED <<entryGen, staged, batch>>

ResetGen ==
  /\ occupant = NONE
  /\ gen > 0
  /\ gen' = 0
  /\ entryGen' = 0
  /\ staged' = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, batch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Read(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Enter(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Work(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Leave(w)
  \/ ResetGen

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<gen, occupant, entryGen, staged, batch>>

OccupantFresh ==
  occupant # NONE => gen = entryGen + 1
====
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch guards one critical ledger section using optimistic locking. A worker reads the current generation counter into its own staged view; a worker may be slow but not failed, so its staged view can lag behind the live generation. A worker enters the critical section only while the section is free and its staged view still equals the live generation; entering records the entry generation and bumps the generation. Inside the section the worker advances the settlement batch. Leaving the section bumps the generation again. When the section is idle, the generation counter may be reset to zero so it does not run away.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a worker occupies the critical section, the live generation is exactly one greater than the generation it entered on, so no second worker is ever inside at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m0p3t3 ----
\* A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates units with optimistic locking. Each unit carries a version
\* whose parity encodes its state: even means free, odd means allocated. A requester first reads a
\* unit's version into its staged view; a requester may be slow but not failed, so its staged view can
\* lag. It allocates the unit only while the unit is free and its staged version still matches the live
\* version, which flips the version to odd; freeing flips it back to even. A stale requester drops its
\* view and re-reads. A unit is recorded as allocated exactly when its version is odd, so a free unit
\* is never handed to two requesters at once.
EXTENDS Naturals

NONE == "none"
Units == {"u1", "u2"}
Requesters == {"q1", "q2"}
MaxVer == 2

VARIABLES holder, ver, staged, target

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in [Units -> Requesters \cup {NONE}]
  /\ ver \in [Units -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ staged \in [Requesters -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ target \in [Requesters -> Units \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ holder = [u \in Units |-> NONE]
  /\ ver = [u \in Units |-> 0]
  /\ staged = [q \in Requesters |-> 0]
  /\ target = [q \in Requesters |-> NONE]

ReadUnit(q, u) ==
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![q] = ver[u]]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![q] = u]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ver>>

Allocate(q, u) ==
  /\ holder[u] = NONE
  /\ target[q] = u
  /\ staged[q] = ver[u]
  /\ ver[u] < MaxVer
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![u] = q]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![u] = ver[u] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, target>>

Free(q, u) ==
  /\ holder[u] = q
  /\ ver[u] < MaxVer
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![u] = NONE]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![u] = ver[u] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, target>>

Retry(q, u) ==
  /\ target[q] = u
  /\ staged[q] # ver[u]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![q] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ver, staged>>

Next ==
  \/ \E q \in Requesters, u \in Units : ReadUnit(q, u)
  \/ \E q \in Requesters, u \in Units : Allocate(q, u)
  \/ \E q \in Requesters, u \in Units : Free(q, u)
  \/ \E q \in Requesters, u \in Units : Retry(q, u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<holder, ver, staged, target>>

AllocParity ==
  \A u \in Units : (holder[u] # NONE) <=> (ver[u] % 2 = 1)
====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates units to requesters using optimistic locking. Each unit carries a version number whose parity encodes its state: an even version means the unit is free, an odd version means it is allocated. A requester reads a unit's version into its own staged view; a requester may be slow but not failed, so its staged view can lag behind the live version. It allocates a unit only while the unit is free and its staged version still equals the unit's live version, which flips the version from even to odd. Freeing a held unit flips the version from odd back to even. A requester whose staged view no longer matches drops it and re-reads.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A unit is recorded as allocated exactly when its version number is odd, so a free unit is never handed to two requesters at once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m4p3t4 ----
\* An air-traffic runway allocator hands flights runways through a bounded request queue with
\* backpressure. Only runways currently in the open set may be allocated, and the open set is grown
\* or shrunk as the operating capacity changes at runtime, never opening a runway that is already
\* assigned. Allocating pulls a queued flight, moves it onto an open runway, and removes that runway
\* from the open set. Releasing frees a flight's runway. An assigned runway is never also listed as
\* open, so a runway is only ever allocated from the open set to a single flight and never
\* double-allocated.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

NONE == "none"
Flights == {"f1", "f2"}
Runways == {"y1", "y2"}
MaxCap == 2
QCap == 2

VARIABLES openRw, assigned, queue, flightRw, capacity

TypeOK ==
  /\ openRw \in SUBSET Runways
  /\ assigned \in [Runways -> Flights \cup {NONE}]
  /\ queue \in Seq(Flights)
  /\ flightRw \in [Flights -> Runways \cup {NONE}]
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
  /\ openRw = {}
  /\ assigned = [r \in Runways |-> NONE]
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ flightRw = [f \in Flights |-> NONE]
  /\ capacity = 1

AdjustCapacity(c) ==
  /\ capacity' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<openRw, assigned, queue, flightRw>>

OpenRunway(r) ==
  /\ r \notin openRw
  /\ assigned[r] = NONE
  /\ Cardinality(openRw) < capacity
  /\ openRw' = openRw \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, queue, flightRw, capacity>>

CloseRunway(r) ==
  /\ r \in openRw
  /\ openRw' = openRw \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, queue, flightRw, capacity>>

Request(f) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < QCap
  /\ flightRw[f] = NONE
  /\ ~\E k \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[k] = f
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, f)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<openRw, assigned, flightRw, capacity>>

Allocate(r) ==
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ r \in openRw
  /\ assigned[r] = NONE
  /\ LET f == Head(queue) IN
       /\ flightRw[f] = NONE
       /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![r] = f]
       /\ flightRw' = [flightRw EXCEPT ![f] = r]
       /\ openRw' = openRw \ {r}
       /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
       /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Release(f) ==
  /\ flightRw[f] # NONE
  /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![flightRw[f]] = NONE]
  /\ flightRw' = [flightRw EXCEPT ![f] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<openRw, queue, capacity>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in 0..MaxCap : AdjustCapacity(c)
  \/ \E r \in Runways : OpenRunway(r)
  \/ \E r \in Runways : CloseRunway(r)
  \/ \E f \in Flights : Request(f)
  \/ \E r \in Runways : Allocate(r)
  \/ \E f \in Flights : Release(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<openRw, assigned, queue, flightRw, capacity>>

OpenAssignedDisjoint ==
  \A r \in Runways : assigned[r] # NONE => r \notin openRw
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator assigns flights to runways through a bounded request queue with backpressure. A runway may be opened into the open set only while it is unassigned and the number of open runways is below the operating capacity, which is adjusted at runtime; a runway may also be closed out of the open set. A flight is queued while the queue has room and the flight has no runway. Allocating takes the head flight and moves it onto a runway that is in the open set and unassigned, recording the assignment and removing that runway from the open set. Releasing frees a flight's runway.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A runway that is assigned to a flight is never also listed in the open set, so a runway is only ever allocated from the open set to a single flight and never double-allocated.

---- MODULE W4Od5m6p3t4 ----
\* A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players in lobby seats under time-limited leases, with
\* the number of seats that may be occupied at once (the capacity) changing at runtime. Claiming a
\* vacant seat hosts a player there and charges the lease to full span, but only while the number of
\* occupied seats is below the current capacity. A lease may be renewed, released, or left to decay
\* one step at a time until it lapses and the seat empties. The vacant-seat set and the seat hosting
\* records are kept coherent: a seat is listed vacant exactly when it hosts no player, so an occupied
\* seat is never handed to a second player.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

NONE == "none"
Seats == {"s1", "s2"}
Players == {"p1", "p2"}
MaxCap == 2
Span == 2

VARIABLES hostedBy, vacant, ttl, capacity

TypeOK ==
  /\ hostedBy \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NONE}]
  /\ vacant \in SUBSET Seats
  /\ ttl \in [Seats -> 0..Span]
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
  /\ hostedBy = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
  /\ vacant = Seats
  /\ ttl = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
  /\ capacity = 1

Occupied == Cardinality({s \in Seats : hostedBy[s] # NONE})

AdjustCapacity(c) ==
  /\ capacity' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hostedBy, vacant, ttl>>

Claim(p, s) ==
  /\ s \in vacant
  /\ hostedBy[s] = NONE
  /\ Occupied < capacity
  /\ hostedBy' = [hostedBy EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ vacant' = vacant \ {s}
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = Span]
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Renew(p, s) ==
  /\ hostedBy[s] = p
  /\ ttl[s] > 0
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = Span]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hostedBy, vacant, capacity>>

Release(p, s) ==
  /\ hostedBy[s] = p
  /\ hostedBy' = [hostedBy EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
  /\ vacant' = vacant \cup {s}
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Decay(s) ==
  /\ hostedBy[s] # NONE
  /\ ttl[s] > 1
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = ttl[s] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hostedBy, vacant, capacity>>

Lapse(s) ==
  /\ hostedBy[s] # NONE
  /\ ttl[s] = 1
  /\ hostedBy' = [hostedBy EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
  /\ vacant' = vacant \cup {s}
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in 0..MaxCap : AdjustCapacity(c)
  \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Seats : Claim(p, s)
  \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Seats : Renew(p, s)
  \/ \E p \in Players, s \in Seats : Release(p, s)
  \/ \E s \in Seats : Decay(s)
  \/ \E s \in Seats : Lapse(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<hostedBy, vacant, ttl, capacity>>

VacancyCoherent ==
  \A s \in Seats : (s \in vacant) <=> (hostedBy[s] = NONE)
====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players in lobby seats under time-limited leases, and the number of seats that may be occupied at once, the capacity, changes at runtime. Claiming a vacant seat hosts a player there and charges the lease to its full span, but only while the number of occupied seats is below the current capacity. A lease may be renewed to full span, released early, or left to decay one step at a time until it lapses and the seat empties. The set of vacant seats and the per-seat hosting records are kept coherent as the seats fill and empty.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A seat is listed as vacant exactly when it hosts no player, so an occupied seat is never handed to a second player.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m0p4t2 ----
\* A wildfire drone surveillance swarm assigns drones from one shared pool to fire zones, driven by
\* two controller instances using optimistic locking. Each zone carries a version and a capacity that
\* shifts as the fire grows or shrinks. A controller reads a zone's version, then assigns a free drone
\* to that zone only while its staged version still matches and the zone's current drone count is below
\* its capacity, bumping the version. Drones may be recalled, and a stale controller re-reads. The
\* number of drones assigned to any zone never exceeds that zone's capacity.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

NONE == "none"
Drones == {"d1", "d2"}
Zones == {"z1", "z2"}
Instances == {"a", "b"}
MaxCap == 2
MaxVer == 2

VARIABLES assignedZone, cap, ver, staged, targetZ

TypeOK ==
  /\ assignedZone \in [Drones -> Zones \cup {NONE}]
  /\ cap \in [Zones -> 0..MaxCap]
  /\ ver \in [Zones -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ staged \in [Instances -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ targetZ \in [Instances -> Zones \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
  /\ assignedZone = [d \in Drones |-> NONE]
  /\ cap = [z \in Zones |-> 1]
  /\ ver = [z \in Zones |-> 0]
  /\ staged = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
  /\ targetZ = [i \in Instances |-> NONE]

Load(z) == Cardinality({d \in Drones : assignedZone[d] = z})

ReadZone(i, z) ==
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![i] = ver[z]]
  /\ targetZ' = [targetZ EXCEPT ![i] = z]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assignedZone, cap, ver>>

Assign(i, d, z) ==
  /\ targetZ[i] = z
  /\ staged[i] = ver[z]
  /\ assignedZone[d] = NONE
  /\ Load(z) < cap[z]
  /\ ver[z] < MaxVer
  /\ assignedZone' = [assignedZone EXCEPT ![d] = z]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![z] = ver[z] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, staged, targetZ>>

Recall(d) ==
  /\ assignedZone[d] # NONE
  /\ assignedZone' = [assignedZone EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, ver, staged, targetZ>>

AdjustCap(z, c) ==
  /\ c >= Load(z)
  /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![z] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<assignedZone, ver, staged, targetZ>>

Next ==

  \/ \E i \in Instances, d \in Drones, z \in Zones : Assign(i, d, z)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Recall(d)

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm assigns drones from one shared pool to fire zones, driven by two controller instances using optimistic locking. Each zone carries a version and a capacity that shifts as the fire grows or shrinks; capacity may be adjusted at runtime but never below a zone's current drone count. A controller reads a zone's version into its staged view, then assigns a free drone to that zone only while its staged version still matches the zone's live version and the zone's current drone count is below its capacity, bumping the zone version. Drones may be recalled from a zone, and a controller whose staged view is stale reads the zone again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of drones assigned to any zone never exceeds that zone's capacity.

\* a node consumes reservation slots up to a capacity that changes at runtime. A node is in the critical
\* section only if it holds the token, and the token rests with exactly one node, so at most one node is
\* ever in the critical section at a time.
EXTENDS Naturals

Nodes == {"n1", "n2", "n3"}
MaxCap == 2

  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==

  /\ inCS = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
  /\ capacity = 1
  /\ used = 0

  /\ token' = Nxt[n]

  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, capacity, used>>

Access(n) ==

  /\ used < capacity
  /\ used' = used + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inCS, capacity>>

Exit(n) ==
  /\ inCS[n]
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, capacity, used>>

AdjustCapacity(c) ==

  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inCS, used>>

  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Enter(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Access(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Exit(n)

---- MODULE W4Od18m0p1t2 ----
\* Two instances share one door-lock configuration record and update it with optimistic locking.
\* An instance reads the record's current version into its staged view, then commits a new setting only
\* while it still holds a live read and its staged version matches the record's version; the commit
\* stores the value, advances the version, and appends the value to the change history. An instance
\* whose staged read has gone stale abandons it and reads again. Because a commit is admitted only on a
\* fresh read, the stored setting always equals the most recently committed value in the history, so no
\* concurrent update is silently lost.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Instances == {"a", "b"}
MaxVer == 2
Vals == {0, 1}

VARIABLES setting, version, hist, staged, reading

TypeOK ==
  /\ setting \in Vals
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
  /\ hist \in Seq(Vals)
  /\ staged \in [Instances -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ reading \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ setting = 0
  /\ version = 0
  /\ hist = << >>
  /\ staged = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
  /\ reading = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]

ReadRec(i) ==
  /\ ~reading[i]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![i] = version]
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<setting, version, hist>>

Commit(i, v) ==
  /\ reading[i]
  /\ staged[i] = version
  /\ version < MaxVer
  /\ setting' = v
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ hist' = Append(hist, v)
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED staged

Abandon(i) ==
  /\ reading[i]
  /\ (staged[i] # version \/ version = MaxVer)
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<setting, version, hist, staged>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Instances : ReadRec(i)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, v \in Vals : Commit(i, v)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : Abandon(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<setting, version, hist, staged, reading>>

SettingMatchesHistory ==
  IF hist = << >> THEN setting = 0 ELSE setting = hist[Len(hist)]
====
nl:
Two instances share one door-lock configuration record and update it with optimistic locking. An instance reads the record's current version into its staged view and marks itself reading. It commits a new setting only while it is still reading and its staged version equals the record's live version; the commit stores the new value, advances the version by one, and appends the value to the change history. An instance whose staged read no longer matches the live version, or which finds no further version available, abandons its read and may read again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The stored setting always equals the most recently committed value in the change history, so no concurrent update is silently lost by a blind overwrite.
